facts.fact_text: According to the applicant, the demonstrations of 31 July 2010 and 10 March 2013 were intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicant, the demonstrations of 31 July 2010 and 10 March 2013 were conducted in a peaceful manner.
According to the applicant, the participants of the demonstration of 31 July 2010 were demanding free and fair elections and democratic reforms in Azerbaijan.
According to the applicant, the participants of the demonstration of 10 March 2013 were protesting over the deaths of numerous soldiers in the army.
The applicant attended the demonstration of 31 July 2010.
The applicant attended the demonstration of 10 March 2013.
Shortly after the demonstration of 31 July 2010 had begun, the police started to disperse those who had gathered.
Shortly after the demonstration of 10 March 2013 had begun, the police started to disperse those who had gathered.
The applicant was arrested during the dispersal operation at the demonstration of 31 July 2010.
The applicant was arrested during the dispersal operation at the demonstration of 10 March 2013.
By a decision of 31 July 2010, the Sabail District Court (first-instance court) convicted the applicant under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).
By a decision of 31 July 2010, the Sabail District Court (first-instance court) sentenced the applicant to seven days' administrative detention.
By a decision of 11 March 2013, the Sabail District Court (first-instance court) convicted the applicant under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).
By a decision of 11 March 2013, the Sabail District Court (first-instance court) sentenced the applicant to seven days' administrative detention.

The administrative offence report issued following the applicant's arrest on 31 July 2010 stated that by deliberately failing to comply with a lawful order of the police, the applicant had committed an administrative offence under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).

Following the applicant's arrest on 10 March 2013, the applicant was charged with an administrative offence under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) (participation in a public assembly organised not in accordance with the law).

At the time of the applicant's arrest on 31 July 2010, Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences 2000 (CAO) provided that deliberate failure by an individual to comply with a lawful order of a police officer or military serviceman carrying out their duties to protect public order shall be punishable by a fine of twenty to twenty-five manats (AZN) or, if that sanction is inadequate in the circumstances of the case and taking into account the character of the offender, by up to fifteen days' administrative detention.

Following the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, participation in an assembly organised in breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies became explicitly punishable under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).
The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) noted that of the locations proposed by the organisers at which to hold the assembly, the squares were all designated public leisure areas.
The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) noted that of the locations proposed by the organisers at which to hold the assembly, the other places (apart from the squares) were areas with heavy traffic.
The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) refused to authorise the demonstration of 31 July 2010 at the places indicated by the organisers.

The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) proposed three alternative locations on the outskirts of Baku for the demonstration of 31 July 2010: a stadium situated in the Binagadi District, a square near Zigh Road in the Khatai District, and the yard of a driving school situated in the 20th habitable area of the Sabail District.
The organisers decided to hold the demonstrations in the centre of Baku despite the Baku City Executive Authority's refusal to authorise the demonstration at the places indicated.
According to the applicant, the demonstrations of 31 July 2010 and 10 March 2013 were intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicant, the demonstrations of 31 July 2010 and 10 March 2013 were conducted in a peaceful manner.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe, titled 'The honouring of obligations and commitments by Azerbaijan', stated that there is no political dialogue with the opposition parties outside parliament in Azerbaijan.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that the Parliamentary Assembly is concerned by the restrictive climate for the activities of the extra-parliamentary opposition in Azerbaijan, which complains about limitations imposed on freedom of expression and freedom of assembly and the lack of access to the public media.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that recently adopted amendments to the Criminal Code and the Administrative Code of Azerbaijan, which increased penalties for the organisers of and participants in 'unauthorised' gatherings, raise concern.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that, considering the Azerbaijani authorities' ongoing blanket ban on protests in the Baku city centre, the amendments increasing penalties for organisers of and participants in 'unauthorised' gatherings are likely to have a further negative impact on freedom of assembly and freedom of expression.

The Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 by Nils Muižnieks, Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, stated that the sanctions which can now be imposed, coupled with the fact that local authorities have not authorised a single rally in Baku city centre in recent years, clearly have a chilling effect on the organisation of or participation in demonstrations in Azerbaijan.

The Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 by Nils Muižnieks, Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, stated that participants in peaceful assemblies should not be sanctioned for the mere fact of being present at and actively participating in the demonstration in question, provided they do not do anything illegal, violent or obscene in the course of it.
